metadata.title: What a Republican 'wipeout' in the midterm elections means for investors

content.text:
Veda Partners managing partner and director of economic policy Henrietta Treyz outlines the type of policy shifts that could affect investors most if the Republicans end up "wiping out" in the midterm elections.
As you said, it looks like a wipeout potentially for the Republicans. If that is does come to pass, what are the investment implications of that?
I'm that's the most important thing. So, the desperate times call for desperate measures. Sorry, I was screaming for my brother at the US Open last night.
Oh.
But uh the the thing that I would be most concerned about in the immediate term for investors is the possibility of an export control or a ban on gas and diesel sometime just before the election.
That would be extraordinarily disruptive. It could temporarily lower domestic gas prices, but on a go-forward basis, it changes the economics of a global commodity. So that's thing number one.
And then thing number two, I think that investors should be wary of the investigations and oversight that Democrats are going to embark upon next year, which is going to be much more private industry focused.
So, you know, you can haul up Pete Hegseth and Kristi Noem and all those cabinet members as much as you want. That's not going to be market moving. What Democrats are looking for is understanding whether Walmart and Dollar Tree and Apple were able to get um tariff rate reductions.
And if they did, if they got an exclusion, which we know that Apple for example did or Tesla, did you send that money back to consumers? When you got the refund, did you lower prices? Or did you not?
Uh why were you granted the exclusion? Is there a quid pro quo with the White House? Did you give money to the ballroom and then get a kickback? What's going on here? So, I think they're going to be interested in hauling up the CEOs of Meta and Google and Nvidia and Apple.
And they're going to have a targeted understanding of if this impacts inflation, if it impacts consumer prices, we want to understand what you're doing, why you've done it and what your coordination is with the White House.
